messages:
mira: Quick follow-up from the UX/RBAC sync — I want to propose removing the UI Edge Shim (the client-side authz layer that replicates server checks) and treat it as deprecated for the console. It’s causing cache divergence, extra round trips, and a few flaky permission edge cases.

alex: Strong +1 on simplification. The shim has been bandaid-y for a long time. Two concerns: (1) customers/tenants that currently rely on shim behavior, (2) rollout safety and rollback plan.

mira: Agreed. My sketch for a phased plan:
- discovery: identify tenants still triggering shim paths via telemetry
- harden: ensure server-side checks are feature-complete (policy parity)
- canary: route a small percent of console traffic to server-only path with fallback window
- cut: full removal after 2 weeks of stable canary
- rollback: flip feature flag to re-enable shim quickly for affected tenants

jordan: Quick question — the original reason was to avoid stale capability tokens and avoid an expensive server hop for simple table navs. How do we keep latency similar?

sam: Two approaches: (A) add a short-lived capability token exchange on first UI load and cache it in browser (ttl ~5m), or (B) optimize the server-side quick-check path (in-memory prefix cache for common perms). I prefer B since A leaks complexity to the frontend and complicates audits.

alex: For canary safety we should do traffic split 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated abort if auth_error_rate increases or p99 latency regresses by >10%. Also add a tenant opt-out tag so Sales can request a hold.

mira: Yes — will add those gates. Draft runbook snippets: 
```
# flip feature flag for canary (console-config service)
PATCH /config/flags HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json
{ "ui_edge_shim": "canary:0.5" }

# quick rollback
{ "ui_edge_shim": "enabled" }
```

mira: Monitoring checks (promql examples):
- auth_error_rate: sum(rate(console_auth_errors_total[5m])) / sum(rate(console_requests_total[5m]))
- p99_latency: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(console_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
- shim_fallbacks: sum(rate(ui_shim_fallbacks_total[5m]))

jordan: Can we add a small feature-flagged telemetry header so we can correlate sessions to shim vs server-only quickly? e.g., `x-console-rollout: shim-vs-server` 

sam: Yep — sidecar will inject `x-console-rollout` and the console API will echo it into logs. ops-bot, can you create the alert on auth_error_rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m during rollout?

ops-bot: created alert: CONSOLE_UI_AUTH_ERROR_SPIKE (severity P2) — triggers on: (sum(rate(console_auth_errors_total[10m])) / sum(rate(console_requests_total[10m]))) > 0.005 

alex: Implementation notes:
- API: add `X-Edge-Shim-Disabled` header fallback for debugging
- Cache: add a small LRU per API worker keyed by (user_id, resource_prefix) with TTL=60s to keep p99 similar without shim
- Rollout docs: update console README and send a short customer notice template for tenants that might be impacted

mira: Timeline proposal: discovery/telemetry (1 week), parity fixes + tests (2 weeks), canary (2 weeks ramp), full cut (1 week hold). Target cutover week: 2024-10-07 (tentative).

jordan: Please add a short compatibility test to the infra repo that fuzzes a few permission combos against server-only path, we saw an ordering bug last time.

mira: Will add test matrix (owned by eng-platform + eng-security). I’ll open a PR with the feature-flag gates, runbook, and the canary schedule today.

alex: Thanks — please @me on the PR. If we keep the canary abort thresholds conservative we should be fine. :thumbsup:

sam: One last ops note: when you flip the flag, also bump the console rollout cookie version so browsers pick up the new behavior without stale js caching.

mira: Good call. Adding that to the runbook. Closing thread for now — will post PR link when ready.
